notes:
NDM 2.3.6 is the release where playlist video stops depending on an external downloader. HLS and DASH streams are now parsed by the engine itself — master playlists, variant selection, segment templates and timelines — and the segments are downloaded by the same multi-connection engine that handles ordinary files, with the same pause, resume, speed limit and progress reporting. yt-dlp remains what it was always best at in NDM: resolving a page to its streams, and the fallback when a playlist is encrypted or live.

Starting the app and starting a download both got more reliable. A second request for a video that is already resolving no longer stacks a fresh long wait on top of the first, a finished resolve no longer leaves its card saying "Resolving…" forever, and the picker's seeded resolutions now warm in parallel instead of one after another. Captures from the browser queue like file offers: one dialog at a time, in order, instead of two or three stacked on top of each other.

Two correctness fixes close holes that could damage files or lock users out. An FTP server that accepts a resume offset and then streams from the beginning anyway — a real behaviour of some broken servers — could silently corrupt a multi-connection download; the probe now proves resume honesty with a byte witness before trusting it, and falls back to a single stream when the proof fails. And files behind HTTP Digest authentication (RFC 7616, MD5 and SHA-256) now download with the site login instead of failing at the password prompt; Digest support did not exist before this release.

The packages now ship THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md covering every bundled crate and runtime component.
